Writing scenarios

Source: vignettes/articles/writing-scenarios.Rmd
writing-scenarios.Rmd

By default a dossier runs the code users learned from the release: its vignettes and its help-page examples. Users also run code that neither shows, such as the README’s example, the answer to an issue, or the analysis in a paper that uses the package. A scenario file adds that code to the dossier. This article covers when you need one, how to write it, and what makes a scenario useful evidence.

What the defaults leave out

from_vignettes() makes each vignette a scenario and each R chunk a step. from_examples() makes each help page with examples a scenario and each top-level expression a step. Neither runs:

  • example code in \dontrun{}, or vignette chunks with eval = FALSE; these are listed as not run;
  • the computation behind vignettes that read stored results (readRDS(), load(), cache = TRUE): they run, but their numbers come from the file, and the report flags them;
  • functions no vignette or example calls. The summary’s coverage line lists the exported functions the scenarios do not use, and says how many NEWS bullets match no step;
  • code users run that your documentation does not show.

To run only some vignettes or help pages, name them: from_examples(which = c("fit_model", "plot_model")).

A scenario file

A scenario file is an R file of scenario() calls, each with its step()s:

# dev/dossier/scenarios.R
scenario("readme", title = "The README's example", source = "README.md",
  step("data", "setup", d <- subset(mtcars, cyl > 4)),
  step("fit", "fit", fit <- fit_model(mpg ~ wt, data = d)),
  step("estimates", "print", estimates(fit), values = TRUE),
  step("plot", "plot", plot(fit), w = 6, h = 4)
)

Here fit_model() and estimates() stand for your package’s functions; the package is attached before the scenarios run, as library(mypkg) would. Keep the file in your repository, in a folder that .Rbuildignore excludes, and add it to the dossier’s scenarios, from the package’s folder:

d <- dossier("mypkg", scenarios = list(from_vignettes(), from_examples(),
                                       scenario_file("dev/dossier/scenarios.R")))
cmp <- run_dossier(d)

The path is read when the dossier runs, relative to the working directory. Then:

  • every scenario() the file creates is used, in the order created. The code in each step() is not run when the file is read: it is kept and run unchanged under each version, in a fresh R process;
  • the steps of a scenario share one environment, so later steps see what earlier ones created. Each scenario starts afresh: options, attached packages, environment variables and the working directory that one scenario sets are put back before the next;
  • the seed is set before every step;
  • scenarios from a file run from the run’s own folder, not from your package’s folder.

Each step has a kind:

Kind What the step adds
"setup" runs, but is not reported: data preparation
"run" console output, warnings, errors and plots, compared
"fit" as "run", and timed with repeats, for the slower and faster labels
"print" as "run", and the printed form of its value, compared on its own
"plot" as "run", with plots drawn at w by h inches

values = TRUE makes a step collect every number and short string in its visible value and in any object it assigns at top level, with the element names users’ code might read (fit$estimates$se). Moved numbers (value_moved) and removed and added elements (field_removed, field_added) are found from these; without them, a step’s results are compared only as printed text. Objects of heavy classes, such as model fits and plots, are not walked (see default_skip_classes()): collect what users read from them, coef(fit) or summary(fit), in a step of its own. Vignette chunks and examples collect values by default; the steps you write collect them only when you say so.

One change, three steps

The small package bundled with pkgdossier, udfixture, has a function make_result() that loses its element b in version 1.1.0. Here is a scenario file that meets this change in three ways, plus one step that uses an argument only 1.1.0 has:

scenario("results", title = "What users read from a result",
  step("assigned", "run", res <- make_result()),
  step("printed", "print", make_result()),
  step("collected", "run", res <- make_result(), values = TRUE),
  step("new_api", "plot", draw(col = "blue"))
)

With the file saved as scenarios.R in the temporary folder, a dossier of the two bundled versions runs it. tarball() takes a source tarball on disk:

fixture <- function(version) {
  system.file("extdata", paste0("udfixture_", version, ".tar.gz"), package = "pkgdossier")
}
d <- dossier("udfixture",
  base = tarball(fixture("1.0.0")),
  candidate = tarball(fixture("1.1.0")),
  scenarios = scenario_file(file.path(tempdir(), "scenarios.R")),
  reps = 0
)
cmp <- run_dossier(d, html = NULL, json = NULL, open = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
summary(cmp)[, c("step", "status", "kinds")]
#>        step      status          kinds
#> 1  assigned        same               
#> 2   printed     changed output_changed
#> 3 collected     changed  field_removed
#> 4   new_api error_fixed    error_fixed

The same change, found three ways:

  • assigned: the result is assigned and never shown, so there is nothing to compare. The step is the same under both versions.
  • printed: the printed list lacks $b. The change is found, as changed output (severity 3).
  • collected: with values = TRUE, res$b is found missing: field_removed, severity 1, which is what it is for users whose code reads res$b.

And new_api: draw(col = ) exists only in 1.1.0, so under 1.0.0 the step errors with “unused argument”, and the dossier reports an error the candidate fixed. That is evidence of nothing. A scenario runs under both versions, so write it with what the release has.

What makes a good scenario

  • Users’ code, unchanged. Copy it as users wrote it, and say where it comes from in source, which the report shows.
  • The release’s functions only. Code that needs the new version shows up as error_fixed, as above.
  • Values where users read results. Use values = TRUE on the steps whose results users’ code takes apart.
  • One step per thing a user looks at. Differences are reported per step, and NEWS bullets are matched to the functions each step uses, so smaller steps place both more precisely.
  • Repeatable. Avoid the clock and the network. Files in your repository are not in the run’s folder: read data shipped with the package through system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "mypkg"), or make it in a "setup" step.

A step that errors under both versions is listed as a scenario problem: it tests nothing, so fix the scenario.

Trying a scenario file

While you write the file, run only it, without timed repeats:

run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", scenarios = scenario_file("dev/dossier/scenarios.R"),
                    reps = 0))

The installed versions are reused between calls; changing the file runs the scenarios again.
